title: GST 111 (COOU) | Chapter One: Listening Skills for Effective Communication, Examination and Research Purposes
subject: GST 111

questions.question: What are the four major language skills?
questions.explanation: The chapter lists listening, speaking, reading, and writing as the four major language skills.

questions.question: Which language skill is the major concern of Chapter One?
questions.explanation: Chapter One focuses on listening skills for effective communication, examination and research.

questions.question: If a listener fails to hear accurately, he acts:
questions.explanation: The text states that if a listener fails to hear accurately, he acts inaccurately.

questions.question: Discriminative listening appears to be traced to:
options: Early stage of a child's life
questions.explanation: Discriminative listening is traced to the early stage of a child's life.

questions.question: Some linguists link discriminative listening to:
questions.explanation: Some linguists link discriminative listening to the womb when the child knows the world of the mother's womb.

questions.question: Discriminative thinking can later lead to:
questions.explanation: The text says discriminative thinking can later lead to sectionalism as one may choose who or what to listen to.

questions.question: Which of the following is a step to effective listening?
questions.explanation: Face-to-face contact is listed as a step to listening.

questions.question: Focusing on the teacher by primary pupils may pose problems of:
questions.explanation: Focusing on the teacher may pose problems of lack of concentration, especially when the teacher dresses amorphously.

questions.question: Primary pupils are advised to focus their gazes on:
questions.explanation: Such pupils are advised to focus their gazes at the chalkboard instead of the teacher.

questions.question: A listener needs to be in an atmosphere of:
questions.explanation: A listener needs to be in an atmosphere of tranquility to guarantee holistic attention.

questions.question: Free mindedness means a listener should keep his or her mind free of:
questions.explanation: A true listener should keep his or her mind free of all thoughts—yesterday, today, or tomorrow.

questions.question: If a listener listens with other imaginations in mind, he is:
questions.explanation: If a listener listens with other imaginations, such a listener is bound to lack concentration and is listening absentmindedly.

questions.question: A good listener should listen with:
questions.explanation: A good listener should listen with soul and body.

questions.question: The essence of listening is to understand what is:
questions.explanation: The essence of listening obviously is to understand what is communicated.

questions.question: A listener must be conversant with the grammar of the speaker's language to understand:
questions.explanation: A listener must be conversant with the grammar of the speaker to understand the content words used.

questions.question: Listen with enthusiasm means the listener must listen with:
questions.explanation: The listener who wants to understand the message must listen with admiration and interest.

questions.question: As a student, you cannot ask a valid question in relation to what has been taught if you had not:
questions.explanation: You cannot ask a valid question if you had not listened well.

questions.question: You must align with the speaker first and understand him before you:
questions.explanation: You must align with him first, understand him before you ask reconciling questions, if necessary.

questions.question: Focus on what you hear implies that a listener should be:
questions.explanation: A listener should be submissive in his listening to understand all that is said.

questions.question: According to the chapter, knowledge comes from:
questions.explanation: The text states that knowledge comes from listening.

questions.question: Sitting properly in class is described as:
options: Sine qua non to good listening
questions.explanation: Sitting properly in class is sine qua non to good listening.

questions.question: Which sitting position may induce sleep?
questions.explanation: Some sitting positions may induce sleep while others may attract unnecessary attention, hampering listening.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the types of listening listed in the chapter?
questions.explanation: The listed types include attentive, focused, evaluative, critical, peripheral, appreciative, emphatic and content; selective is not listed.

questions.question: Whenever a listener acts contrarily to what is said, he can be said to have listened but not:
questions.explanation: Whenever a listener acts contrarily to what is said, he can be said to have listened but not emphatically.

questions.question: Attentive listening means listening to what is being said with:
questions.explanation: A good listener is supposed to listen to what is being said soul and body.

questions.question: Focused listening is differentiated from attentive listening because the focused listener wants to:
questions.explanation: The focused listener may be listening to get a particular point, while the attentive listener wishes to hear all quietly.

questions.question: The evaluative listener is described as:
questions.explanation: The evaluative listener is a skilled or intelligent listener who can always make conclusions after listening.

questions.question: Critical listening is almost the same as:
questions.explanation: Critical listening is almost the same as evaluative listening because both allow the listener to assess and make judgments.

questions.question: The critical listener must also be an:
questions.explanation: The critical listener must also be an attentive listener who listens to capture all that has been said.

questions.question: Peripheral listening is not:
questions.explanation: Peripheral listening is not holistic and summative; the listener listens only to what he wants to hear.

questions.question: Emphatic listening can also be called:
questions.explanation: Emphatic listening can also be called active listening because the listener still responds to others even while listening.

questions.question: Emphatic listening may be problematic because the listener may:
questions.explanation: Emphatic listening may be problematic because the listener may at a time lose his focus and so listening and understanding become ineffective.

questions.question: Content listening means listening to understand:
questions.explanation: Content listening is listening to understand whatever is said or taught.

questions.question: According to Sitti and Shalawati, factors influencing students' listening skills include lack of practice, limited vocabulary mastery, native speakers' accent and:
questions.explanation: The five factors include lack of practice, limited vocabulary mastery, native speakers' accent, and pronunciation.
